reason: The observations are accurate but the finding is out of scope and its fix is forbidden by the brief. Verified by driving the master: state=day reads Today / Mara & Finn / Saturday 3 October 2026 / 'Everything on the plan has happened. Nothing is left to count.' plus the foot, and a regex sweep for clock times across all eleven states returns nothing. But the reason there is no time, address or contact is that there is none in the data: REVIEW_TIMELINE_MILESTONES in src/lib/review-suite-fixture.ts is typed { sourceId, publicId, title, date, state } with date-only strings, and the lab's fixture.js mirrors it verbatim. The brief bars the remedy twice over: 'the data model' is named in What is out of scope, and the Fixture section says 'Never placeholder text, never a hand-rolled imitation of the data.' Every concrete element of the proposed fix -- an optional time and place per item, '2.00pm - The Orchard, Adare', a fixture day plan ordered by clock time, a venue address, one named contact -- is invented content plus a schema change. Building it would trade the one property this seat itself calls the biggest win (every number derived from the real dates through one accessor, so picture and words cannot drift) for a screen of fiction. The print half fails on its own terms too: the lab pins a single review clock, 2026-07-16, and every surface states that today, so the A4 printed on 16 July honestly shows 79 days; the brief lists 'a printer' and 'the morning of the day itself' as separate surfaces (DIRECTIONS.md), and re-clocking print to the wedding morning would break the one-clock discipline to fix a scope the brief does not set. The claim that the product 'has nothing to say' on 3 October is also overstated against the direction's own record: REFERENCE.md indicts the current product with 'The day itself does not exist. Nothing in the product changes on 3 October', and B answers that with a dedicated composition where the countdown resolves. Whether that composition is too spare is a taste argument the finding does not make; the argument it does make requires data that does not exist.
sharpenedFix: If the panel wants anything on this element, only this is in constraint and it is small: rebuild state=day from facts the fixture already holds rather than adding any. The screen currently drops every string that anchors the day -- it never names 'Wedding day at The Orchard', which every other surface carries, and it shows none of the nine things that got the couple there. In-scope version: keep 'Today', the names and the long date, then set the place line under the rule from PROJECT.primaryDate.label plus the existing Orchard string, and render the completed plan beneath it as the quiet keepsake list the same behind() accessor already produces. Also revisit the sentence 'Everything on the plan has happened' -- the Wedding day milestone is dated 3 October, so on that morning it has not happened; the copy is true only under the code's daysTo(x) <= 0 bucketing. No new field, no new fixture, no invented time or address.
